name: 3do-adndslayer-doc
description: AD&D Slayer (3DO, 1994) documented from a CHD: 151,340 sectors all attributed, 87.6184 % identified, 67.4093 % uncompressed AIFF, the ANIM container walked (370 files, 2,516 frames), a twin whose OS differs by 68 bytes, and a pressing date in /rom_tags. Credits decoded, counted, not transcribed.

name: 3do-aloneinthedark-doc
description: Alone in the Dark (3DO, Europe, 1994): the first disc in five whose sector map does not close. 14.83 % of it is two other computers -- 34 MB of a PC's Watcom C/C++ 10.0 at the end of the pressing, 24 MB of a Macintosh build machine inside the files. Coverage moved 49.00 % to 90.79 %.

name: 3do-crashnburn-doc
description: Byte-level measurements of Crash 'n Burn (3DO, Crystal Dynamics, 1993), the first 3DO disc in this collection. An Opera file system reader written from scratch; 451 files, not the 326 a mis-read next_block field showed; 7,239 frames of a codec the studio wrote because Cinepak had not shipped.

name: 3do-doctorhauzer-doc
description: A Japanese 3DO CD-ROM of April 1994 that presses a third of itself twice. 80 files with up to seven copies, 90,050,560 bytes of duplicated content against a platform rule, and the unit of duplication is a contiguous run of files across directories. Eight Cinepak films, 77 IMAG images, 1,157 cels, and the game's script in plain Shift-JIS.

name: 3do-fifainternationalsoccer-doc
description: One retail 3DO CD-ROM, measured: FIFA International Soccer (Europe), 1994. 63.35 % of it is 43 Cinepak films of 1960s-80s World Cup footage - 19,597 frames at exactly 15 fps, all decoded. Data Streamer with no SHDR. Two studio formats derived. No product bytes.

name: 3do-gamelist-doc
description: Index of the 3DO disc documentation: one repository per pressing, plus the shared Opera-filesystem platform checklist they feed into. Empty so far - created before the first disc so that disc one has a structure to be filed into. Format archaeology only, no disc images, no game assets.

name: 3do-omf2097
description: A playable port of One Must Fall: 2097 to the Panasonic/3DO, built on OpenOMF

name: 3do-platformnotes-doc
description: The canonical 3DO platform checklist, to be carried across documentation pipelines: the Opera filesystem at sector 0 (not ISO 9660), ARM6 big-endian code behind LaunchMe, CELs and Cel Control Blocks, SDX2 audio and the Data Streamer. A scaffold - every claim is marked [unverified] until a disc says otherwise.

name: 3do-superstreetfighter2turbo-doc
description: A 3DO CD-ROM read from the volume label up: 86.2465 % of it is recorded music, 733 Cel Control Blocks derived from the bytes, and the second disc of the platform, opened to find out which of the first disc's findings were about the 3DO and which about one studio.

name: 3do-wolfenstein3d-doc
description: Wolfenstein 3D (3DO, USA, 1995) read end to end: 56,702 sectors, 197 files, 59.79 % recorded audio. The Data Streamer the 3DO checklist had marked dead for two discs, decoded frame by frame - and its codec is Cinepak, spelled 'cvid' in lower case. Six two-disc rules broken.

name: 3dokit
description: A toolkit for 3DO ports: Opera discs, AIF executables, an ARM60 static recompiler to C++ and a Portfolio OS runtime (cels, DataStream, audio, DSP). No game data.

name: 7800kit
description: Atari 7800 reverse engineering and static recompilation: an NMOS 6502-to-C++ recompiler and a MARIA runtime under it; the whole library runs native, frame-identical to the interpreter.

name: android-dissidiaduellum-doc
description: The Android data directory of DISSIDIA FF / DISSIDIA DUELLUM, pulled off a live phone and documented while the service still runs: 729 UnityFS archives opened and validated, 683,378 objects, and an answer to why a client announcing 2.6 GB left 3.79 GB on disc.

name: android-talesofcrestoria-doc
description: File-format and engine documentation for Tales of Crestoria (Bandai Namco, Android, 2020-2022), built on tri-Ace's ASKA engine: SLZ/Zstandard containers, ISF packages, ETC2 textures, Cocos Studio UI, Ogg Vorbis audio, GLSL shader archives, and a hollowed-out native library.

name: android-talesofluminaria-doc
description: Tales of Luminaria (Android, 2021) — file formats, engine and protection, measured from the shipped package. Unity 2019.4.16f1 + IL2CPP, COLOPL, project 'natalie'; not ASKA, and nothing in common with Tales of Crestoria.

name: apple2-gamelist-doc
description: Index of the Apple II game documentation: one repository per title, measured from disk images - p-System volumes spread over floppies, DOS 3.3 disks as publishers filed them, what the programs keep and what players left. Documentation only - no game assets.

name: apple2-theoregontrail-doc
description: The Oregon Trail (Apple II, MECC, v1.4 1987), two disk sides: DOS 3.3 with label entries, a loader reading 135 sectors by address, 39 closed Applesoft programs on a 46-command & toolkit, a saved variable table, 23 packed screens and 70 images, 20 tunes, the Top Ten and tombstones players left (described, not quoted).

name: apple2-wizardryiv-doc
description: Wizardry IV: The Return of Werdna (Apple II, 1987), six disk sides: a 1 MB directory spread over five floppies by SYSTEM.RELOC (239 of 239 shared blocks identical), the Huffman text decoded to 424 messages, 15 level maps and D-I-N-K, the Mordorcharge table, three interpreter builds, and a sixth side called BLANK.

name: bpc-emu
description: Emulator for the Benesse Pocket Challenge V2 (2000s), the WonderSwan-based study handheld of the Shinkenzemi courses: drop a cartridge and play. All 13 dumped cartridges reach their drills and questions, cycle-identical to a WonderSwan reference interpreter. Bring your own dumps.

name: casiolator
description: Emulator for Casio's two cartridge consoles, the PV-1000 (1983) and the Loopy (1995): drop a cartridge and play. PV-1000 complete with sound; every Loopy cartridge starts, clean-room SH-1, VDP and sound chip; tools for English fan translations (work in progress). Bring your own dumps.

name: cd32-alfredchicken-doc
description: Alfred Chicken (Twilight / Mindscape, Amiga CD32, 1993): structural documentation read from an original pressed disc, the first physical one in this set. Settles that the thirteen-zero CATALOG is the mastering not the dumper, that the overrun past the declared volume is cut into the glass master, and verifies MODE1/2048 by descrambling.

name: cd32-banshee-doc
description: Reverse-engineering notes on Banshee (Core Design, 1994) for the Amiga CD32: a same-label control against Dragonstone, a 640x512 HAM8 picture nothing runs, RNC ProPack method 2 inside an executable, and a debug hook in the shipped boot script

name: cd32-dragonstone-doc
description: Reverse-engineering notes on Dragonstone (Core Design, 1995) for the Amiga CD32: disc layout, RNC ProPack, the AmigaDOS boot chain, three-language text, and the leftovers -- a cut level, a floppy prompt, and an Exec object file in sector 21.

name: cd32-fireandice-doc
description: Structural documentation of the Amiga CD32 release of Fire & Ice: The Daring Adventures of Cool Coyote (Graftgold / Renegade, 1994) - ISO 9660 layout, PowerPacker 2.0 containers, copper-driven AGA display, cd.device use, and the leftovers of its floppy ancestry. Documentation only, with Python tools that reproduce every figure.

name: cd32-gamelist-doc
description: Index of the Amiga CD32 / CDTV disc documentation: one repository per pressing, each with the full per-disc write-up, plus a link to the shared platform checklist they all feed into. Format archaeology only - no disc images, no game assets.

name: cd32-gloom-doc
description: Reverse-engineering notes on Gloom (Black Magic Software / Guildhall, 1995) for the Amiga CD32: a chunky texture-mapped renderer that never touches Akiko, because its framebuffer is a copper list with one MOVE per pixel

name: cd32-guardian-doc
description: Reverse-engineering notes on Guardian (Acid Software, 1994) for the Amiga CD32: a polygon engine that fills every scanline with one Blitter cookie-cut into four interleaved bitplanes, a 24-bit per-scanline copper sky, and Akiko measured to zero for the eleventh time

name: cd32-gunship2000-doc
description: Structural documentation of Gunship 2000 (MicroProse, 1994) on Amiga CD32: a 100 MiB zero hole, an unreachable Pirates! Gold demo, little-endian IFF, and 542 validated RNC2 streams. Documentation only.

name: cd32-heroquest2-doc
description: Reverse-engineering notes on HeroQuest II: Legacy of Sorasil (Gremlin, 1994) for the Amiga CD32 — RNC ProPack 1 with a rotating XOR key, a hunk file that decrunches and relocates itself in 584 bytes, and an ECS display on AGA silicon with Akiko measured to zero.

name: cd32-jamespond2-doc
description: James Pond 2: Codename RoboCod (Amiga CD32, 1993) — measurements of the pressed disc: a 128.000000 MiB hole, 93.9 % of the file bytes as CDXL video, a three-language manual with no characters in it, and a boot script that is a signed development diary. Nineteenth disc in the CD32 set.

name: cd32-legends-doc
description: Reverse-engineering notes on Legends (Krisalis Software, 1996) for the Amiga CD32: a six-floppy A1200 game on a CD, a Bytekiller decruncher, a hand-written LoadSeg, and the developers' photographs

name: cd32-liberation-doc
description: Liberation: Captive II (Byte Engineers/Mindscape, 1994, Amiga CD32) — the largest CD32 data track in the series, 91 % of it speech: three Wyvern shared libraries that are the 3D engine, 10,792 pre-rendered wall sprites instead of a texture mapper, three generators run at boot, and a text system that shipped with its author's note to translators

name: cd32-marvinsmarvellousadventure-doc
description: Reverse-engineering notes on Marvin's Marvellous Adventure (21st Century Entertainment, 1994/1995) for the Amiga CD32: disc layout, Puzzle V2.0 level format, planar graphics, in-house music modules, CDXL intro, and a great deal of leftover development material.

name: cd32-microcosm-doc
description: Reverse-engineering notes on Microcosm (Psygnosis, 1994) for the Amiga CD32: 92% of the data track is one 483 MB video file of 30,707 frames, decoded straight into 8 AGA bitplanes. Documentation only.

name: cd32-myth-doc
description: Structural teardown of Myth: History in the Making (Amiga CD32, System 3). The disc is the 1992 three-floppy release pressed whole - three 880 KiB disk images plus an 18 KB shim - behind a hole of exactly 50 MiB. Bytekiller under the magic DAVE, a hand-written LoadSeg, an Akiko CD driver, and a PVD date the disc itself falsifies.

name: cd32-platformnotes-doc
description: The canonical Amiga CD32 / CDTV platform checklist, carried from one documentation pipeline to the next: disc identification, the trademark block at sector 21, the AmigaDOS epoch, RNC ProPack, hunk executables, copper lists and planar bitmaps.

name: cd32-powerdrive-doc
description: Power Drive (CD32): a 1992 rally game pressed by Myth's mastering house with the same stuck 1992-12-21 clock and 50-MiB hole; 583 planar car frames closed from the bytes; Akiko drives the CD and NVRAM, and the C2P port is zero even register-relative

name: cd32-prey-doc
description: Reverse-engineering notes on Prey: An Alien Encounter (Almathera / KirkMoreno Multimedia, 1993) for the Amiga CD32 — an hour of speech streamed as 1,225 identical 60 KB files, no audio track, and the disc that says where the Commodore trademark block's exec fragment came from

name: cd32-superfrog-doc
description: Structural documentation of the Amiga CD32 release of Superfrog (Team 17, 1994). A compilation master: the game plus Super Stardust and Arcade Pool demos. The 1993 three-floppy layout recovered exactly from the CD binary; the resident band ceiling broken by 0.64 %; cruncher follows the label, .TM block follows the tool.

name: cd32-thesperislegacy-doc
description: Structural documentation of The Speris Legacy (Amiga CD32, 1996, Binary Emotions / Team 17): the Imploder decruncher taken out of the game, the LEV2 level format rendered, the copy-protection code tables reconstructed, and a CD32 disc carrying the CDTV .TM block.

name: cd32-universe-doc
description: Structural documentation of the Amiga CD32 release of Universe (Core Design, 1994): a 16-opcode bytecode interpreter, RNC ProPack nested three levels deep, 602 KB of four-language script, Akiko's CD-ROM and I2C EEPROM ports driven by hand, and an ECS display on AGA silicon.

name: cdi-avisittosesamestreetletters-doc
description: A Visit to Sesame Street - Letters (Philips CD-i, September 1991), measured from a raw 2,352-byte-per-sector image: 13,138 DYUV frames decoded, a publisher bumper byte-identical to a disc a year younger, and the executable it replaced still on the pressing.

name: cdi-burncycle-doc
description: Burn:Cycle (Trip Media / Philips Media, CD-i, May 1995) — a film with a program inside it: 7 directory entries, 99.23 % of the volume in one real-time file, RL7 at 384x240 and 12.5 fps decoded, 77:49 of ADPCM the pressing tags as video, and 22 Italian strings

name: cdi-gamelist-doc
description: Index of the Philips CD-i disc documentation: one repository per disc, each with the full per-disc write-up, plus a link to the shared Green Book platform checklist they all feed into. Format archaeology only - no disc images, no game assets.

name: cdi-laserlords-doc
description: Laser Lords (Philips CD-i, 1992) measured from a raw 2352-byte-per-sector image: 290,955 sectors, 33 files, 81 subheader quadruples, ten jukebox streams carrying 6h34m of speech, and the 5,229,000-byte head-region recording that turns out to be a year older than anyone had it

name: cdi-linkthefacesofevil-doc
description: Reverse-engineering notes on Link: The Faces of Evil (Animation Magic / Philips Interactive Media, 1993): CD-i Green Book filesystem, OS-9/68000 executables, real-time streaming, CLUT7 playfields, RL7 animation, ADPCM - and the 325 C function names the retail build still carries.

name: cdi-merlinsapprentice-doc
description: Reverse-engineering notes on Merlin's Apprentice (Philips CD-i, 1995): the linker symbol file that shipped on the retail disc, the BOLT asset container mapped to the byte, and the 27 named puzzles it gives up.

name: cdi-origami-doc
description: Reverse-engineering notes on Origami (Philips CD-i, EagleVision 1993): Green Book file system, OS-9/68000 modules, multi-channel real-time files, DYUV/CLUT7 video, Level B/C ADPCM, and a fifth language nobody catalogued.

name: cdi-platformnotes-doc
description: The canonical Philips CD-i platform checklist, carried across documentation pipelines: Green Book filesystem, OS-9/68000 modules, real-time streaming, DYUV/CLUT/RL7, ADPCM - and the 29 seconds of authoring-system audio that turns up byte-identical on unrelated 1993 discs.

name: cdi-theapprentice-doc
description: Reverse-engineering notes on The Apprentice (Philips CD-i, The Vision Factory, 1994): a CD-i Ready disc hiding the whole game in track 1's pregap, with the linker's symbol table, a shipped 68000 disassembler, and a soundtrack pressed twice.

name: cdi-ultracdisoccer-doc
description: Reverse-engineering notes on Ultra CD-i Soccer (Krisalis / Philips Interactive Media, 1997): CD-i Green Book filesystem, OS-9/68000 executable, CLUT and rlspr graphics, ADPCM audio, the MPEG-1 intro, the 75-team database - and 5.2 MB of scrambled audio the game never reads.

name: cdinet
description: A web browser for the Philips CD-i, through a proxy on the serial port - in the spirit of CD-Online / Web-i

name: cdipc
description: Emulator for the Philips CD-i (220 F2, Magnavox 200) with the Digital Video cartridge: drop a disc and play. Clean-room SCC68070, MCD212, CDIC and MPEG-1 decoders; CD-i titles, MPEG games and Video CDs play. Bring your own dumps.

name: chiproll
description: Browser-based piano roll for chip music. NES and Atari TIA, no install.

name: coleco-ff
description: Final Fantasy (NES, 1987) rewritten in C for the ColecoVision with the Super Game Module and a 512 KB MegaCart. Work in progress: power-on to the bridge. Bring your own assets.

name: dc-dinocrisis-doc
description: Dino Crisis (Italy), Dreamcast GD-ROM, Capcom 2000: the IP.BIN boot block is 99.69 % shared with the first disc, 276 untagged .DAT opened to the byte, and six languages on a disc where 'italiano' counts zero.

name: dc-gamelist-doc
description: Index of the Sega Dreamcast disc documentation: one repository per pressing, plus the shared GD-ROM platform checklist they feed into. Empty so far - created before the first disc so that disc one has a structure to be filed into. Format archaeology only, no disc images, no game assets.

name: dc-lba2
description: Sega Dreamcast port (KallistiOS) of the original 1997 Adeline source of Little Big Adventure 2 / Twinsen's Odyssey. V0.9 alpha — only the opening + first-island transitions are validated on Flycast; real-DC boot blocker pending UART diagnosis. See README-DC.md.

name: dc-platformnotes-doc
description: The canonical Sega Dreamcast platform checklist, to be carried across documentation pipelines: GD-ROM's two areas, IP.BIN in front of the filesystem, the scrambled SH-4 executable, CRI and Sega middleware, PowerVR textures and the ARM7 AICA driver. A scaffold - every claim is marked [unverified] until a disc says otherwise.

name: dc-sonicadventure-doc
description: Sonic Adventure (Dreamcast, 1999, MK-51000) measured from a three-track BIN/CUE GD-ROM: 1ST_READ.BIN is not scrambled, .PRS is LZ77 with no Huffman and closes on 843/843, 17,083 textures, 4,197 ADX streams totalling 5h46m, two ARM7 sound drivers, 244 credited names behind the compressor.

name: didjemu
description: Emulator for the LeapFrog Didj (2008), the LF1000 Linux learning handheld: all 16 known titles start and play, with sound, movies and 3D. The games' own ARM code and LeapFrog's Lightning libraries run on Unicorn; the Brio system services and OpenGL ES are reimplemented on the host. Bring your own dumps.

name: dos-platformnotes-doc
description: A checklist for the MS-DOS-era subset of the PC family, assembled from a sweep of 49 finished repositories

name: ds-lba
description: Little Big Adventure (1994) ported to the Nintendo DS, from the GPL engine source release. 50 fps on a stock 4 MB DS, with voices, streamed music and a touch-screen panel. Bring your own game data.

name: ecliptic
description: Emulator for the Tapwave Zodiac (2003), the Palm OS 5 handheld game console: HLE of Tapwave Native Applications (ARM on Unicorn, TwGlue OS table on the host, 68k launch code on a small PACE layer). Bring your own assets.

name: fcf-bufo
description: BUFO - a road-and-river crossing game for the Fairchild Channel F (1976), written from scratch in F8 assembly. 2 KiB cartridge, 64 bytes of RAM.

name: fcf-quest
description: A JRPG for the Fairchild Channel F (1976). 4 KiB cartridge, 64 bytes of RAM, F8 assembly, written from scratch.

name: flick
description: Mattel HyperScan emulator: the five retail games with sound, RFID cards and two players (work in progress)

name: fmtownskit
description: A kit for native PC ports of FM Towns and FM Towns Marty games: their 386 code statically recompiled to C++, on a runtime of the machine (BYOA)

name: gamewave-doom
description: Doom as a ZAPiT Game Wave game script (Lua on the console's own ZIT engine), developed in the Undertow emulator

name: gc-talesofsymphonia-doc
description: Structural documentation of Tales of Symphonia on GameCube (2003, two discs) and PlayStation 2 (2004, one disc): the 1995 Wolf Team block codec on a big-endian console, the first source edit to its decoder since 1997, and the gigabyte the two-disc split cost.

name: hs-lba
description: Little Big Adventure (1994) ported to the Mattel HyperScan: S+core 7 at 108 MHz, 16 MB, a servo-driven CD, and 96 bytes of save on an RFID trading card. Bring your own assets.

name: hyperscan-homebrew
description: Technical documentation & homebrew research for the Mattel HyperScan (S+Core 7): 16+ GCC score-elf compiler bugs, PPU/RFID/I2C drivers, and the first emulated HyperScan audio in MAME.

name: jag-lba
description: Little Big Adventure (1994) ported to the Atari Jaguar, from the GPL engine source release: 640x480 interlaced, 3D bodies on the GPU, all 120 scenes in a 6 MB cartridge. Work in progress. Bring your own assets.

name: keitai-talesoftactics-doc
description: Structural documentation of the Tales of Tactics i-appli trial (NTT DoCoMo DoJa, 2004): the Tales block codec measured absent across 2.47 MB and 37,936 constants, a full class file parser in the Python stdlib, and a five-title crossover party table.

name: mame
description: MAME

name: mobigoemu
description: Emulator for the VTech MobiGo (2010), the GeneralPlus u'nSP learning handheld: drop a cartridge and play. Touch screen, keyboard and sound; every cartridge tried reaches its menus, several their games; the undocumented ADPCM36 sound format worked out from the cartridges. Bring your own dumps.

name: n64-lba2
description: Little Big Adventure 2 (Twinsen's Odyssey) native Nintendo 64 port of the original 1997 engine, on libdragon. Bring your own assets.

name: nds-talesofhearts-doc
description: Byte-level documentation of Tales of Hearts (Nintendo DS, Namco Bandai, 2008) — both cartridges. The Tales block codec is absent across 33 modules, 32 of them BLZ-packed; FPS4 crosses from Tales of Vesperia little-endian; 28,662 of 28,679 payloads identical between the two editions.

name: nds-talesofinnocence-doc
description: Structural documentation of Tales of Innocence (Nintendo DS, 2007, Japan): the control that shows the Tales block codec's absence on the DS is about the codebase, not the machine — it compresses 16.9 MB into 32.1 MB in the platform's own LZ77.

name: nds-talesofthetempest-doc
description: Tales of the Tempest (Nintendo DS, 2006, Japan): the Tales block codec is absent, and so is every other compressor — the ARM rewrite of the constant scan, 256 MB run blind, and a cartridge 41% empty that stores its data raw.

name: ndskit
description: A game-agnostic toolkit for Nintendo DS reverse engineering and native PC ports: cartridge images, an ARM/Thumb decoder, a static recompiler to C++ (programs and overlays), and a runtime that replaces the DS's hardware (both ARM CPUs, the 2D and 3D engines, the sound unit). No game data.

name: ngpc-dreamcast-link-cable
description: A virtual Neo Geo Pocket Color <-> Dreamcast link cable between two emulators (patched beetle-ngp + Flycast BattleCable). Retail MOTM <-> MF2K upload works. BYOA.

name: ngpc-homebrew-notes
description: Homebrew notes for the SNK Neo Geo Pocket Color (TLCS-900H), including the first NGPC<->Dreamcast link-cable bridge ever emulated.

name: pasogo-emu
description: Emulator for the Koei PasoGo (1996), the handheld Go machine built on a Vadem VG230 'PC on a chip': drop a cartridge and play. The three dumped cartridges reach their menus and play; NEC V30 and VG230 written from scratch from the chip's manual and the cartridges' own BIOS. Bring your own dumps.

name: pc-1000miglia-doc
description: Measurements of 1000 Miglia (MS-DOS, 1991-92): 124 files, one flat directory, and what an installed BBS distribution can and cannot say about a product

name: pc-3ddotgameheroes
description: Towards a native PC port of 3D Dot Game Heroes (PS3, 2009): a static recompilation on ps3kit, with the disc's formats documented. BYOA, no game data.

name: pc-4ddriving
description: Native PC port of 4D Driving (Stunts on the FM Towns Marty, Electronic Arts Victor, 1993) by static recompilation of its 386 code, on fmtownskit (BYOA)

name: pc-883d-doc
description: Measurements of the 883 'Grazie mille' CD Extra data session (Italy, 1999): a Director 7 program, a slot machine, and an Activeworlds chat client whose world server address survived in a cache directory name.

name: pc-abelsmt
description: Native PC port of ABEL - Shin Mokushiroku Taisen (Family Soft, FM Towns, 1995) by static recompilation of its 386 code, on fmtownskit, to be translated into English (BYOA)

name: pc-academagia-doc
description: Academagia: The Making of Mages, the Steam installation: 1,598 files and 352,246,696 bytes of which 360 are distinct. A .NET game whose content is a published Firebird dump: info.bin and header.bin close at residue 0 on 449,320 objects, the twelve files with no magic are the Music slot, and SizeOnDisk is short by seven.

name: pc-ageofwonders2-doc
description: Age of Wonders II: The Wizard's Throne (PC, 2002) measured from the retail CD: a closed form for 143,595,520 bytes of padding, a volume descriptor that names the disc's first and last unreadable sector, and the first two files shared between two different publishers in this collection.

name: pc-albertodyssey
description: Toward a native PC port of Albert Odyssey: Legend of Eldean (Sega Saturn, 1997) by static recompilation, built on saturnkit: playable from the boot to the harpies' village. BYOA: documentation and tools only.

name: pc-allodsonline-doc
description: Allods Online (build 13.505, eng_eu): a byte-level study of 1,186 files and 17,366,372,506 bytes downloaded over BitTorrent. 9,148 of 9,148 SHA-1 pieces verified, 871 of 871 manifest hashes, an archive ownership map closing to zero, 2.88M words, 29 h of sound, and a layer written by the machine it is installed on.

name: pc-arcrisefantasia
description: Toward a native PC port of Arc Rise Fantasia (Wii, 2009): disc and code analysis, a stripped executable recompiled, a gamepad or the keyboard as the Classic Controller, on wiikit. BYOA.

name: pc-baronbaldric-doc
description: Baron Baldric: A Grave Adventure (MS-DOS, Manaccom, 1992-93): the .BNK container, a Turbo Pascal linker map shipped by accident, a 256-stride sprite codec, and thirteen timestamps forty-eight years in the future

name: pc-battlebugs-doc
description: Format documentation for Battle Bugs (Sierra/Epyx, 1994, MS-DOS): resource containers, the 16-colour planar image codec, level and sprite layout, and the XMIDI/DIGPAK audio stack

name: pc-bianconatale-doc
description: BIANCO NATALE (Tecnoart, Genova, MS-DOS, 1994): 18 files measured. A Christmas platform game that is 95% raw pixels behind two undocumented formats, and a third of which advertises the studio. Lowest opening coverage this collection has measured, 4.8838%.

name: pc-bloodandlace-doc
description: Measuring the Blood & Lace disc (GMM Entertainment, Tortona, 2001): a Nero master, a signed engine licence inside japotek3d.dll, and a chapter-by-chapter comparison with its sibling Zero Comico, which shares the engine seven months later.

name: pc-brokensword3-doc
description: A read-only measurement of a GOG install of Broken Sword: The Sleeping Dragon (2003). 6,748 files, 1.72 GB, zero duplication. Both GOG manifests reconciled and 6,736 MD5 verified; data.pak opened (19,751 members, no gaps); 6,721 RenderWare streams shown to be 4-bit ADPCM. Thesis: 71.2028 % sound and film.

name: pc-brokensword4-doc
description: A read-only measurement of a live GOG installation of Broken Sword: The Angel of Death (2006). The three EmPackFi archives opened: 17,978 members, 58.4 % compiled 3D scenes that date themselves, Emmersion 3449:0, amBX 1073:0, and 291 members shared with Broken Sword 3.

name: pc-brokensword5-doc
description: A GOG install of Broken Sword 5 (2014) measured byte by byte: 33 files, 6.6 GB, two undocumented container formats derived and proved, 71,938 members censused, and an engine whose universally-attributed name occurs zero times in the object.

name: pc-bumpy-doc
description: BUMPY'S ARCADE FANTASY (Loriciel, MS-DOS, 1992) from a 1992 Fairlight download folder: the 12-byte big-endian codec read out of the unpacked loader and closed on 38 of 38 files, 14 screens rendered, 9 levels of 126 platforms, 511 sprites, a manual-lookup copy protection and its two-byte crack.

name: pc-canediterracotta-doc
description: Il cane di terracotta (2000), a hybrid PC/Mac CD-ROM measured on both filesystems: Windows sees 2,374 files in 4 folders, the HFS volume holds 2,401 in 11, and 2,372 of the 2,373 they share begin on the same sector. Director 7.0.2, a 10,240-byte grid with a closed form at 100%, and a Windows 95 stack leaked into 517 Macintosh audio files.

name: pc-capcombeatemupbundle-doc
description: Measurements of Capcom Beat 'Em Up Bundle (PC, Steam, 2018): 268 files, 809,632,531 bytes. Derives the ARC/IBIS/TEX/GMD containers, resolves 13 of 13 MT Framework type hashes, identifies all four regions of all 14 arcade ROMs, and answers 'whose emulator' with a measured non-answer.

name: pc-castlevaniajudgment
description: Toward a native PC port of Castlevania Judgment (Wii, 2008): a stripped executable named from a kin and recompiled on wiikit, the stages' fog, the save kept, a gamepad as the Classic Controller. BYOA.

name: pc-celltosingularity-doc

name: pc-twinsensquest-doc
description: A GOG offline installer measured as an object: 2 files, 2,891,523,108 B, 100.0000 % placed with residue 0. Inno Setup 5.6.2 Unicode over a shop naming layer derived here -- 788 files it would write, never run. Five content descriptors. 101 of 101 script opcodes of the 1994 original in the 2024 assembly.

name: pc-underground-doc
description: Underground (PC, Tecniche Nuove, 1999): a Nero-burned CD-ROM measured to the byte. 61.0193 % is 24.9 s of rendered film at a data rate no 1999 drive could serve; the BANK archive format and a Microsoft Video 1 decoder derived from the bytes; four authors credited only in pixels.

name: pc-victorious
description: Toward a native PC port of Victorious: Taking the Lead (Wii, 2012): disc and code analysis, a static recompiler, and wiikit, a game-agnostic Wii toolkit. BYOA.

name: pc-virtualhydlide
description: Toward a native PC port of Virtual Hydlide (Sega Saturn, 1995): disc and code analysis, all 15 programs recompiled to C++, the game's own sound drivers on an emulated 68000 and SCSP, 60 pictures a second from its 12 fps logic, on saturnkit. BYOA.

name: pc-wackywheels-doc
description: File-format and engine documentation for Wacky Wheels (Beavis Soft / Apogee, 1994): the WACKY.DAT archive, the tiled 2048x2048 world, the sprite banks, and the fixed-point look-up tables behind its software pseudo-3D floor renderer. Documentation only, no game assets.

name: pc-wizardry-doc
description: Seven files and 329,541 bytes: a self-booting UCSD p-System disk that never calls DOS. Its volume header declares 1,272 blocks and the file holds 640, and the 212 blocks it calls ZOT contain none of it. Four bytes of a 1987 interpreter say Take.

name: pc-xjapan
description: Toward a native PC port of X JAPAN Virtual Shock 001 (Sega Saturn, 1995) by static recompilation, built on saturnkit: playable from the boot to the backstage. BYOA: documentation and tools only.

name: pc-zerocomico-doc
description: Zero Comico (Windows, GMM Entertainment / Medusa Games, 2001) documented from the bytes: two in-house containers wrapping a 1989 LZHUF stream, 69.49 % of the CD spent on 13 minutes of all-keyframe Indeo video, an engine still carrying a cancelled game, and a retail executable whose version resource says Playable Demo. No assets.

name: pippin-homebrew
description: Networking the Bandai Pippin @WORLD under emulation: upstreamable DingusPPC serial/DBDMA fixes that put the emulated Pippin on the real Internet, plus a homebrew thin-client browser.

name: ps1-talesofdestiny-doc
description: Structural documentation of Tales of Destiny (PlayStation, SLPS-01100, 1997): the disc, the executable, the LZSS codec it inherited from the Super Famicom Tales of Phantasia, and the file system compiled into the program.

name: ps1-talesofeternia-doc
description: Structural documentation of Tales of Eternia (PlayStation, Japan, SLPS-03050 disc 1): the block codec that is byte-identical to 1997's, 90 MB of duplicated sprite sheets, the whole JIS level 1 font inside the executable, and a developer debug room shipped on the retail disc.

name: ps2-talesofdestiny2-doc
description: Structural documentation of Tales of Destiny 2 (PS2, SLPS-25172, 2002): the 1995 Tales block codec still running a console generation later, an archive index that packs padding into its offsets, the whole overlay map recovered from the linker, and 173 MB of an unreleased game shipped with every file stubbed to one byte.

name: ps2-talesoflegendia-doc
description: Structural documentation of Tales of Legendia (PlayStation 2, 2005, SLPS-25533): the block codec present with 1997's ring constant but no inherited source, a sixteen-byte CPS envelope replacing the corpus's nine-byte block, 4,508 of 4,508 members decoded, and a 1 GB unreferenced build artefact.

name: ps2-talesofrebirth-doc
description: Structural documentation of Tales of Rebirth (PlayStation 2, SLPS-25450, 2004, Japan): three headerless .BIN containers indexed from the executable, 744 SCPK bundles, 2,851 codec blocks, and the measurement showing Wolf Team's LZSS decoder had forked per title by 2004.

name: ps2-talesoftheabyss-doc
description: Structural documentation of Tales of the Abyss (PlayStation 2, 2005, SLPS-25586): the Tales block codec's nine-byte header restored after Legendia's CPS, 47,513 of 47,513 blocks decoding, and a decoder that shares 69 bytes with the one copy of Symphonia's source nobody edited.

name: ps2kit
description: A game-agnostic PlayStation 2 toolkit: disc images, executables, the EE decoder, its own static recompiler to C++ and a runtime (kernel, IOP, IPU, GS) for native PC ports

name: ps3-talesofxillia-doc
description: Structural documentation of the Japanese PlayStation 3 disc of Tales of Xillia (2011): the Tales block codec is on neither of the Cell's two instruction sets, TO11 is the game's root C++ namespace, the TL engine is one codebase from 2009 to Berseria in 2017, and the region table claims an encryption that is not there.

name: ps3kit
description: A game-agnostic toolkit for native PC ports of PS3 games: the executable's structure, Cell PPU and SPU decoders, a static recompiler to C++, and a runtime that replaces the PS3's system software. No game data.

name: psx-lba
description: Little Big Adventure (1994 DOS engine) ported to the PlayStation, at its native 640x480. Bring your own assets.

name: saturnkit
description: A game-agnostic toolkit for Sega Saturn reverse engineering and native PC ports: disc images, an SH-2 decoder, a static recompiler to C++, and a runtime that replaces the Saturn's hardware (both SH-2s, VDP1, VDP2, SCU, SMPC, CD block, the 68000 and the SCSP). No game data.

name: silicon-relics
description: Silicon Relics — a living codex of retro console homebrew, reverse engineering and porting quests, from the famous to the forgotten.

name: snes-rudranohihou-re
description: Reverse-engineering devlog of the Japanese text system of Rudra no Hihou / Treasure of the Rudras (SNES, Square). Methodology + tooling, no ROM/assets.

name: snes-talesofphantasia-doc
description: Structural documentation of Tales of Phantasia on SNES (1995) and GBA (2003): ExHiROM mapping, the in-house LZSS block codec, the SPC700 boot payload, and what the GBA rebuild inherited from the cartridge.

name: tales-blockcodec-doc
description: The Tales block codec, documented once: Wolf Team's in-house LZSS on the Super Famicom (1995) and the PlayStation (1997), with a reference decoder for both dialects.

name: tales-gamelist-doc
description: Index of the Tales series documentation: one repository per title, spanning cartridges, discs, a keitai i-appli and a phone gacha, plus the shared Wolf Team block codec they all feed into. Documentation only - no game assets.

name: tg16kit
description: PC Engine / TurboGrafx-16 reverse engineering and static recompilation: a HuC6280-to-C++ recompiler and a VDC/VCE/PSG runtime under it; the whole HuCard library runs native, frame-identical to the interpreter.

name: undertow
description: Emulator for the ZAPiT Game Wave Family Entertainment System (HLE of the ZIT Lua engine)

name: vis-fileviewer
description: Media file viewer for the 1992 Tandy/Memorex VIS — browse and play a CD's photos, OPL3 audio (WAV/MIDI) and Autodesk FLC video, the native Modular Windows way on an 80286.

name: vis-gamelist-doc
description: Index of the Tandy/Memorex VIS disc documentation: one repository per pressing, plus the shared platform checklist they feed into. Three retail discs in hand, none documented yet. Format archaeology only - no disc images, no game assets.

name: vis-linksthechallengeofgolf-doc
description: Links: The Challenge of Golf (Access Software, 1992) for the Tandy VIS, measured from the bytes. Nine archives of an undocumented container opened: 320 members, residue 0, an LZW identified from nineteen uncompressed RIFF members. GIFM is a GIF. 197 of 197 members byte-identical to the MS-DOS release. Fifteen chapters, four new tools.

name: vis-platformnotes-doc
description: The canonical Tandy/Memorex VIS platform checklist: Modular Windows on an 80286, Win16 NE titles, the CONTROL.TAT vendor block whose leading 84 bytes are byte-identical across three unrelated discs, DispDib and the OPL3/DAC audio paths. Three provenance marks - retail-disc, authoring-side, and SDK-only - kept deliberately separate.

name: vis-racetheclock-doc
description: Race the Clock (Tandy, 1992) for the Tandy/Memorex VIS, measured from the bytes. 1,208 Video for Windows files on a platform where AVI was thought unsupported; 80.2861 % of the disc is copies of itself; a 136,192-byte Win16 NE importing HC.HCCONTROL by name. Nineteen chapters, five new tools, one hash list.

name: vis-sherlockholmes-doc
description: Byte-level documentation of Sherlock Holmes: Consulting Detective Vol. I (Tandy/Memorex VIS, 1992, ICOM Simulations). 96.4344% of the disc is .IMV, a video format with no published description: derived, decoded, 1h48m at 15fps with 22,050 Hz PCM interleaved. And a retail VIS disc with no Windows executable at all.

name: vis-synth
description: OPL3 polyphonic synth for the Tandy/Memorex VIS (1992) — pad-driven instrument, SMF MIDI file player, and live MIDI from host hardware via custom MAME bridge

name: vis-thesecretsofhoseafreeman-doc
description: A Tandy VIS CD-ROM nobody could identify: a treasure hunt through a New Bedford whaling house and museum. Derives RIFF/ANIM, the platform's third moving-picture format; names PLAYBACK.DLL's exports; finds an Apple II inside 26 bytecode scripts. 19 chapters, 70 predictions scored.

name: vis-wolf3d
description: Homebrew port of Wolfenstein 3D to the Tandy/Memorex Video Information System (VIS, 1992) — Win16 native, OPL3 audio, MAME-tested

name: vs-sr-dev
description: Silicon Relics — cross-console preservation research and homebrew for obscure vintage platforms.

name: watarakit
description: Watara Supervision reverse engineering and static recompilation: a W65C02-to-C++ recompiler and the runtime under it; the whole library runs native, frame-identical to the interpreter.

name: wii-talesofgraces-doc
description: Structural documentation of the Japanese Wii disc of Tales of Graces (2009): the Tales block codec is on it, 138 bytes shared with the 2003 GameCube decoder, project tag TO10, a Nintendo DS ROM inside the disc, and the first build of this line that names its developer.

name: wii-talesofsymphoniadotnw-doc
description: Structural documentation of Tales of Symphonia: Ratatosk no Kishi (Wii, 2008, Japan): the Nintendo build from inside the studio line that closes the Tales block-codec boundary — 10 bytes of shared decoder with its 2003 GameCube prequel against 835 of shared SDK code, while the same compressor still writes both discs' archives.

name: wii-thelaststory-re
description: Reverse-engineering notes and tools for the LastWorld engine of The Last Story (Wii, 2011). Code and documentation only - no game assets.

name: wiikit
description: A game-agnostic toolkit for Wii reverse engineering and native PC ports: disc images, executables, a Gekko decoder, a static recompiler to C++, and a runtime that replaces the Wii's hardware. No game data.

name: wiiu-crema
description: Crema: a clean-room GX2/AX engine for Wii U homebrew - benchmarked on real silicon

name: wiiu-lba2
description: Wii U port of Little Big Adventure 2 / Twinsen's Odyssey — original 1997 Adeline source (2.21/LBALab community release), completed start-to-finish on real hardware. See README-WIIU.md

name: wiiu-planetblupi
description: Homebrew Wii U port of Planet Blupi (Epsitec / D. Roux) — GamePad touch = mouse, runs on Aroma. GPLv3+

name: wskit
description: Bandai WonderSwan / WonderSwan Color reverse engineering and static recompilation: a V30MZ-to-C++ recompiler and a display/sound/cartridge runtime under it; the whole library runs native, frame-identical to the interpreter.

name: xbox360-talesofvesperia-doc
description: Structural documentation of Tales of Vesperia (Xbox 360, 2008, Japan): XGD2, XEX2, the FPS4 container, and the 1995 Tales block codec still running in August 2008 beside Microsoft's XCompress. Analysis only.
